entries.title: I Kings 19:2
segments:
So let the gods do to me; let them kill me, if I do not kill thee. 
 
No miracles or means of grace will of themselves lead persecutors and haters of God to cease from their efforts to overcome and destroy his people.

entries.title: I Kings 19:3
segments: However bold, courageous, and successful the people of God may have been under his influence, unless that is of God may have been under his influence, unless that is their duty, and in despair even wish to die.

entries.title: I Kings 19:4
segments: Into the wilderness; which lay south of Canaan, and in which Israel had wandered forty years.

entries.title: I Kings 19:5
segments: God knoweth the frame of his people and remembereth that they are dust. He compassionates their infirmities and sympathizes in their sorrows, and when they duly feel their weakness and wants, appears for their relief.

entries.title: I Kings 19:8
segments:
Forty days and forty nights; being miraculously supported. 
 
  Horeb; where God appeared to Israel and gave them the law.

entries.title: I Kings 19:9
segments: Men are made not merely to be acted upon but to act, and should never voluntarily go where they have nothing to do, or can do nothing.

entries.title: I Kings 19:10
segments:
Jealous for the Lord; desirous of honoring him by leading the people to obey him. 
 
  I only; no other prophet openly appeared to stem the torrent of iniquity. 
 
Men are never more likely to boast of their past labors, than when they are neglecting their present duty; nor ever more likely to complain, find fault with others, and sink into despair.

entries.title: I Kings 19:11
segments:
vv 11-12. 
 
  The Lord was not in the wind--earthquake--fire; indicating that he would not reform Israel by terrific outward displays of his power, but by the quiet persevering labors of his servants, under the invisible and silent influences of his Spirit.

entries.title: I Kings 19:12
segments: It is not always that which is most visible and tangible, or which makes the most noise, that is most efficacious in doing good.

entries.title: I Kings 19:15
segments: If the people of God, when fearful, discouraged, and desponding, would get out of trouble, they must go to work; what their hands find to do, they must do for the purpose of honoring God and doing good, committing themselves and all their interests to his guidance and disposal.

entries.title: I Kings 19:16
segments: Abel-meholah; a town in the plain of Jordan, between Beth-shean and Shechem.

entries.title: I Kings 19:17
segments: Hazael--Jehu--and--Elisha; they would all be instrumental in the punishment of idolatrous Israel.

entries.title: I Kings 19:18
segments:
Seven thousand; who were still worshippers of Jehovah. 
 
Some good men are at times tempted to think that there are none who labor in the right way to sustain the cause of God but themselves, and that when they are gone it must sink.  But he will show that it is not as dependent on them as they thought it was.

entries.title: I Kings 19:19
segments: Cast his mantle upon him; indicating that he should follow him.

entries.title: I Kings 19:20
segments:
Go back again; probably said to try the firmness of his purpose. 
 
God can at any time so touch the hearts of men that they will voluntarily and cheerfully leave all for him and his cause.  But in doing this, he will not lessen their natural affection, or lead them to neglect any of the proper kindnesses and courtesies of life.

entries.title: I Kings 19:21
segments:
Took a yoke of oxen; to provide for himself and friends a feast before he left them. 
 
  Ministered unto him; waited on and assisted him.
